title: A Reason Left on the Deletion
story: The studio inbox let anyone delete a client message. After a booking vanished during a tidy, Sen required every deletion to keep the sender, the time, and a reason. Staff called the extra fields slow and unnecessary. The next missing note was rebuilt from those fields in minutes. Speed had been erasing the only history a client could ask them to prove.

vocabulary.definition: The shared place where messages arrive
The act of removing a message
The separate boxes of information that were saved
Put back together from the saved details
Removing something so it cannot be recovered

quiz.question: What could any staff member do to a client message at first?
options: Delete it
Rebuild it from a written reason
Keep it for the client forever by rule
Send it only to the studio owner
quiz.explanation: The inbox let anyone delete a client message.
quiz.supportingSentence: The studio inbox let anyone delete a client message.

quiz.question: What did Sen require a deletion to keep?
options: The sender, the time, and a reason
Only the client’s telephone number
A paper copy of every booking
The fields staff had already refused
quiz.correctAnswer: The sender, the time, and a reason
quiz.explanation: Every deletion had to keep the sender, the time, and a reason.
quiz.supportingSentence: After a booking vanished during a tidy, Sen required every deletion to keep the sender, the time, and a reason.

quiz.question: Why could the next missing note be rebuilt so quickly?
options: The saved fields still held enough detail to reconstruct it
Staff had stopped deleting messages entirely
The client brought a paper copy within minutes
Speed had created a second inbox
quiz.correctAnswer: The saved fields still held enough detail to reconstruct it
quiz.explanation: The note was rebuilt from those fields, so the required details made the recovery possible.
quiz.supportingSentence: The next missing note was rebuilt from those fields in minutes.

quiz.question: What does vanished mean in this passage?
options: Disappeared from the inbox
Grew slower to type
Was proved by the client in court
Was rebuilt the same afternoon
quiz.explanation: The booking vanished during a tidy, meaning it disappeared from the messages.
quiz.supportingSentence: After a booking vanished during a tidy, Sen required every deletion to keep the sender, the time, and a reason.

quiz.question: Why does the writer end by saying speed had been erasing history?
options: To show the cost of deleting without a record
To prove clients never asked for proof
To suggest a tidy inbox is always safer
To argue that reasons should stay blank
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the cost of deleting without a record
quiz.explanation: The last line names what the old speed had destroyed: the history a client might need proved.
quiz.supportingSentence: Speed had been erasing the only history a client could ask them to prove.
